title: The Killing Hands
subtitle: Through the unconscious efforts of many, it has finally completed its mission.

items.text: The Killing Hands
Dikke returned to the grimy room.
A persistent smell of burning tar covered a hint of decay, set against the old files on the shelves, created a somber dread-filled backdrop.
Malachi's heartfelt confessions, wine-soaked as they were, proved more helpful than he likely knew.
"Click—"
She pressed against a concealed stone button.
The secret table revealed itself, along with a neatly arranged assortment of knives and clamps, holding faint traces of dried blood.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Hmm?
A solitary notebook lay on the stone table.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: This is the complete notebook.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: "As for preventing another outbreak of the great plague..."

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: "The disease seems to spread most readily through rats or perhaps fleas... the scent of the patients' corpses and these creatures carry a similar odor..."

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: "...The tower's state of decay has permitted the presence of many vermin which might carry the disease. A thorough cleansing of the tower would seem a prudent move..."

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: "Testing method... senses far beyond those of a normal person... body immune to infection..."

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: "...It is true, I am a wizard, but please trust me, my intentions are pure..."

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: "I just don't want a repeat of the tragedy of this plague."
She closed the notebook.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: So ... not a ghoul, but an arcanist.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: A wizard, fearful of being discovered ... shunned and reviled by everyone. Yet, you continued your work from the shadows. Only for them to call you a ghoul.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: No one appreciates what you've done.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Was this the result you envisioned?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: But, no matter how righteous or noble your intentions were...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Dissecting corpses is a serious violation of the Church's dictates, an indefensible act, Brother Chester.
The flaming sword rested on the stone table, leaving scorch marks on its surface.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: But in any case, your crime did not merit your death.
After a while, she opened up a record, one she had long carried but before now left unfolded.
The monastery was filled by an eerie quiet.

items.speaker: Civilian
items.text: Father, will we find salvation?

items.speaker: Clergy
items.text: Of course, my child, all you must do is pray sincerely.

items.speaker: Civilian
items.text: But we've been praying, yet still my family is bedridden...

items.speaker: Civilian
items.text: They are pious, Father... They have put unwavering trust in our merciful Lord.

items.speaker: Clergy
items.text: Yet, the duty to pray is ours ... and you have not forgotten yours, have you?

items.speaker: Civilian
items.text: So... what should I do? Please, tell me, Father.

items.speaker: Clergy
items.text: We will need a pure silver coin. Heed me, it must not be mixed with copper or iron...

items.speaker: Clergy
items.text: A pure gold coin would be better still ...

items.speaker: Clergy
items.text: Bring it here, and drop it into the redemption box. Reciting your prayers as you do.

items.speaker: Clergy
items.text: When you hear a clear ringing sound, you will know your prayers have been heard.

items.speaker: Civilian
items.text: ...And if there's no sound?
The priest laid a hand gently on his shoulder.

items.speaker: Clergy
items.text: Then that's simple... you haven't offered enough.

items.speaker: Civilian
items.text: But father, will this heal my family?

items.speaker: Clergy
items.text: Perhaps something stronger is needed ... bring to us a ream of parchment, on it we will write our prayers for your kin. Oh- uh, mind you—fine parchment.

items.speaker: Clergy
items.text: After reciting the prayer ... and dropping your coin, we will return the transcribed parchments to you, cut and ground into a powder.

items.speaker: Clergy
items.text: Dissolve it in water and have your family drink it.

items.speaker: Civilian
items.text: Thank you for guidance, Father.

items.speaker: Clergy
items.text: May the Lord bless you.
The faithful man bowed his head, reciting his instructions earnestly.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Frankly, I loathe these records.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: They exist only to stubbornly cling to memories, more of a burden than an aid.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Such outdated things.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: They should have been discarded long ago.
Tossing aside the old documents, she stood up.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: "Render unto Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and unto God the things that are God's."
TO BE CONTINUED…
